## Authoring guide: from a graph to admitted rows

The documentation build renders this guide, the complete SDK/format API tables and
`docs/api/SHARDFILE.md` (every schema field and script ABI call). The examples
below are retained TypeScript sources: the documentation test typechecks and
executes them. They reduce Template 1's hall, door/wave and grey blob to the
smallest useful examples; additional mode/profile examples are explicitly
illustrative data, not changes to Template 1's shipped tuning.

Use real three.js `Scene`, `Group`, `Mesh`, `InstancedMesh`, geometry, materials,
lights and transforms. SDK objects add game declarations to that graph and emit
data. `generators/` and `data/` use the authoring SDK. A shard uses one shard
format; runtime modules use the game's published `plugin/*` modules. Remaining
SDK `runtime/*` exports are compatibility APIs. No imports install
a service. A successful leaf parse does not prove that the complete product's
assets, references, collider clearance, budgets or gameplay have been admitted.

### Format contracts and JSON Schemas

`@wildshard/format/<module>` contains the defining Valibot schemas, types and pure
parsers. It depends only on Valibot. Parse rows before writing them; unknown
fields, invalid bounds and cross-field references refuse. The SDK's
`formatJsonSchema(schema)` produces Draft 2020-12 structural editor data from a
known defining schema. `formatJsonSchemas()` returns the migrated root documents;
`pnpm gen` writes them under `.wildshard/format/`. Named
`x-wildshard-checks` and UTF-16 string bounds still require the defining parser.
JSON Schema validation alone is not the admission verdict. The registry includes
player `modes`, authored `moverMotion` and executable `movers`, including their
component profiles and named mandatory semantic checks. Material-dependent
whole-shard declarations remain outside format until DS1.4.

```ts
import { Director } from '@wildshard/sdk/director';
import { DirectorStagesSchema, parseDirectorStages } from '@wildshard/format/directorStages';
import { formatJsonSchema, schemaAt, schemaDeclaration } from '@wildshard/sdk/formatJsonSchema';
import { ShardfileSchema } from '@wildshard/format/shardSchema';

/** A structural editor schema plus the defining admission verdict for Template 1's first stage. */
export function formatExample() {
  const row = new Director({ id: 'template.door-wave', inputs: {}, stages: [{ id: 'door' }] }).toJSON();
  const declaration = schemaDeclaration(ShardfileSchema);
  const spawn = schemaAt(declaration, '/properties/spawn/wrapped/properties');
  const ui = schemaAt(declaration, '/properties/ui');
  return { schema: formatJsonSchema(DirectorStagesSchema), declaration, spawn, ui, row: parseDirectorStages(row) };
}
```

### Scene graphs and scene.json

Build the hall with ordinary hierarchy operations. Give objects stable names;
place collision and player starts explicitly. A visible `Mesh` is not a collider.
`readScene(scene)` reads the graph in Node; `restoreSceneGraph(description)`
restores its ordinary three.js objects and SDK declaration classes after JSON
transport. Local recipes are retained separately from world-space compiler rows,
so parent transforms apply once. Entries (including Portal and SocketLift),
colliders, spawns, audio, movers and mode objects retain their defining classes.
Neither function
draws or installs gameplay. Instanced transforms, ordered skeleton joints and
inverse binds, named animation tracks and SDK game-concept sections are retained.
Unsupported shear/reflection, nonfinite values and unsupported texture/material
paths refuse. Capsules require uniform scale; entries and player starts keep
upright unscaled frames. Material/look authoring beyond this neutral floor waits
for DS1.4.

```ts
import { Scene, Group, Mesh, BoxGeometry, MeshStandardMaterial } from 'three';
import { BoxCollider } from '@wildshard/sdk/physics';
import { PlayerStart } from '@wildshard/sdk/spawns';
import { Entry } from '@wildshard/sdk/entries';
import { readScene } from '@wildshard/sdk/scene';
import { restoreSceneGraph } from '@wildshard/sdk/sceneGraph';

/** Template 1's named floor, collision, player start and four midpoint entries. */
export function sceneExample() {
  const scene = new Scene(), hall = new Group(); hall.name = 'template.hall';
  const floor = new Mesh(new BoxGeometry(8, 1, 12), new MeshStandardMaterial());
  floor.name = 'template.floor'; floor.position.y = -0.5;
  const collider = new BoxCollider(8, 1, 12, 'stone');
  collider.name = 'template.floor.collider'; collider.position.copy(floor.position);
  const player = new PlayerStart(); player.name = 'template.start'; player.position.set(0, 2, 0);
  hall.add(floor, collider); scene.add(hall, player, ...Entry.midpoints());
  try {
    const data = readScene(scene);
    const restored = restoreSceneGraph(data);
    return { data, restored: readScene(restored) };
  } finally { floor.geometry.dispose(); floor.material.dispose(); }
}
```

### Synth CLI and build outputs

A local `shard.config.ts` exports `scene` (a real three.js graph) and
`identity = { slug: 'template-pilot' }`. From the repository, run
`pnpm exec wildshard synth <project-directory>`. It writes inspectable
`.wildshard/cache/template-pilot/scene.json` and an immutable SHA-256 copy beneath
that directory. `synthScene(scene, projectDirectory, slug)` is the equivalent
programmatic operation; the directory must exist. Then `wildshard build
<project-directory>` builds the declared shardfile project. Synth alone does not
produce an admitted `shard.json`, a card or an entry proof. Keep the readable
TypeScript generator; scene.json is a cache output, not committed source.

```ts
import { Scene, Group } from 'three';
import { synthScene } from '@wildshard/sdk/synth';

/** Publish a Template-style graph into an existing author project directory. */
export function synthExample(project: string) {
  const scene = new Scene(), hall = new Group(); hall.name = 'template.hall'; scene.add(hall);
  return synthScene(scene, project, 'template-pilot');
}
```

### Bake readers: rigs, clips and images

Pass retained authored GLB bytes to `readRigRest` and `readRigMotion`. The former
returns mesh-local geometry, ordered model-space rest joints and the embedded
colour image; dispose its geometry when finished. The latter returns original
three.js `AnimationClip`s and named local node transforms, without a live mixer.
The rest reader admits one triangle skin/primitive; multi-skin composition must
be authored explicitly. Motion supports LINEAR/STEP, and refuses CUBICSPLINE,
morph animation and unsupported integer animation channels. No resampling is
implicit. `readImagePixels`/`writeImagePixels` operate on bounded RGBA images in
Node; the writer emits lossless PNG. The example consumes a real retained GLB,
not a made-up skeleton; supply a separate animation GLB as the second argument
when its clips live in another authored input. Author-tool image support is not shipped texture
admission: render textures still use the admitted KTX2 path. Shared figure-model
adoption remains an open graphical quality pass.

```ts
import { readRigRest, readRigMotion } from '@wildshard/sdk/bake/rig';
import { readImagePixels, writeImagePixels } from '@wildshard/sdk/bake/image';

/** Read a retained authored figure/arm GLB without a page, GPU or live animation service. */
export async function readersExample(glb: Uint8Array, animationGlb = glb) {
  const rest = await readRigRest(glb);
  try {
    const motion = await readRigMotion(animationGlb);
    const image = await readImagePixels(rest.colourImage);
    const png = await writeImagePixels(image);
    const decoded = await readImagePixels(png);
    return { bones: rest.bones, clips: motion.clips.map(clip => clip.name), image, decoded };
  } finally { rest.geometry.dispose(); }
}

/** A public author proof plan; run it against a data-only product whose beacon quest files beacon.lit. */
export function authorProofExample() {
  return { version: 1 as const, tape: Array.from({ length: 120 }, () => []), checkpointTick: 60, requiredFacts: ['beacon.lit'] };
}
```

### Directors: stages and the when-language

`Director` authors a version-2 ordered stage machine. Put `toJSON()` rows in the
root `directors` array (at most 16). Inputs bind existing `flag:`, `zone:`,
`event:` or `actor:<id>.dead|present` owners; the row does not create those owners.
The actual Template 1 door/wave uses quest-owned flags. Its initial stage is
unconditional. The next stage's `when` controls advancement; an explicit `next`
can be a stage id or an ordered array of `{ target, when }`, with the first true
guard selected. Explicit cycles retain their declared order. Stages/actions are
never sorted.

`director.attachTo(scene)` also retains the data-only Director in a named graph
node for scene.json transport. Restoration recreates it as
`node.userData.director`; the Director keeps its existing row `toJSON()` API.
This is an author declaration, not a runtime stage-host installation.

Conditions admit aliases, `true`, `false`, `!`, `&&`, `||` and parentheses with
normal boolean precedence. For example `doorOpen && !waveDead`; there are no
calls, comparisons or arbitrary JavaScript. Limits are 16 inputs, 64 stages,
32 actions per stage, 1024 condition characters, 128 tokens and 16 nested levels.
Missing aliases/targets and a conditional initial stage refuse before installation.

```ts
import { Director } from '@wildshard/sdk/director';
import { generateDirectorAbi } from '@wildshard/sdk/directorAbi';
import { Scene } from 'three';
import { readScene } from '@wildshard/sdk/scene';

/** The actual Template 1 door/wave declaration, with the host-provided flags. */
export function directorsExample() {
  const director = new Director({
    id: 'template.door-wave',
    inputs: { doorOpen: 'flag:template.door-open', waveDead: 'flag:template.blob' },
    stages: [
      { id: 'door' },
      { id: 'wave', when: 'doorOpen', do: [{ flag: { key: 'template.wave-started', value: true } }] },
      { id: 'complete', when: 'waveDead', do: [{ flag: { key: 'template.wave-complete', value: true } }] },
    ],
  });
  const scene = new Scene(); director.attachTo(scene);
  return { row: director.toJSON(), assemblyScript: generateDirectorAbi(director.toJSON()), scene: readScene(scene) };
}

/** Observe the declared look clock's dusk interval without author-side ticks or arithmetic. */
export function dayDirectorExample() {
  return new Director({ id: 'outpost.dusk', inputs: { dusk: 'day:0.75..0.84' }, stages: [
    { id: 'waiting' }, { id: 'lit', when: 'dusk', do: [{ flag: { key: 'outpost.beacon-ready', value: true } }] },
  ] }).toJSON();
}

/** Supported handoff: a director requests a declared flag; the existing quest owner completes it. */
export function beaconRequestExample() {
  const director = new Director({ id: 'outpost.beacon', inputs: { dusk: 'day:0.75..0.84' }, stages: [
    { id: 'waiting' }, { id: 'requested', when: 'dusk', do: [{ flag: { key: 'outpost.beacon-request', value: true } }] },
  ] });
  const quests = { flags: ['outpost.beacon-request', 'outpost.beacon-complete'], triggers: [], dialogue: [], quests: [{
    id: 'outpost.beacon', title: 'Light the beacon', completeFlag: 'outpost.beacon-complete',
    steps: [{ id: 'request', objective: 'Request the beacon at dusk', done: { all: ['outpost.beacon-request'] } }],
    onComplete: { fact: 'outpost.beacon-lit' },
  }] };
  return { director: director.toJSON(), quests, unsupported: director.dataHostIssues() };
}
```

The eight actions have these exact data forms. Each names an already-declared
owner or subscriber; admission of syntax grants no spawn/reward authority.

| Action | Data | Owner's responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| spawn | `{ spawn: 'template.wave' }` | Spawn the declared actor/group. |
| despawn | `{ despawn: 'template.wave' }` | Retire that declared actor/group. |
| flag | `{ flag: { key: 'template.wave-started', value: true } }` | Set a declared quest/state flag. |
| score | `{ score: 'template.score' }` | Select an admitted score. |
| weather | `{ weather: 'template.clear' }` | Select admitted weather data. |
| toast | `{ toast: 'template.tip' }` | Deliver a declared presentation event. |
| reward | `{ reward: 'template.reward' }` | Apply a declared gameplay reward. |
| emit | `{ emit: 'template.wave', value: 1 }` | Emit a bounded number/boolean (default 0). |

For AssemblyScript, `generateDirectorAbi(row)` generates `inputs`, `clock.tick`,
`clock.dt`, `clock.self`, `incomingEvents.count` and `incomingEvents.type(index)`.
Version-2 inputs are booleans; version-1 numeric inputs stay f64. Author source
imports `inputs` and `clock` from `./wildshard-director`; never hand-write memory
offsets. `behaviour/build.json` selects the row through its module's optional
`director` path; `wildshard build` supplies the generated module while compiling
the retained `behaviour/*.as` source. Module hashes come from the compiler's real
bytes. The existing AS handler and host decide how outputs select actions; a
stage row alone does not invent that handler. This small accessor proves the
boolean input module compiles; a playable handler still needs the declared host
exports/actions, not just an accessor.

```ts
import { compileBehaviourModule } from '@wildshard/sdk/buildBehaviour';
import { generateDirectorAbi, generateScriptModule } from '@wildshard/sdk/directorAbi';
import { directorsExample } from './directors';

/** Compile an actual boolean accessor over Template 1's declared input ABI, without inventing a handler. */
export async function directorScriptExample() {
  const source = 'import { inputs } from "./wildshard-director";\nexport function ready(): bool { return inputs.doorOpen && !inputs.waveDead; }';
  return compileBehaviourModule(source, 1, { 'wildshard-director.ts': generateDirectorAbi(directorsExample().row) });
}

/** A complete beacon handler with typed buffers and state; actor identity comes from its native binding. */
export function numericScriptExample() {
  const state = { version: 1, sharedOwner: 'host', playerKey: 'actorId',
    shared: [{ id: 9, name: 'beacon-lit', type: 'bool', privacy: 'public', default: false }],
    player: [{ id: 3, name: 'coins', type: 'i32', privacy: 'owner', default: 0, min: 0, max: 10 }] };
  const module = generateScriptModule(state, `
    if (incomingEvents.count > 0 && incomingEvents.type(0) == 7) {
      shared.beaconLit = true;
      player.coins = player.coins + 5;
      effects.event(7, i32(clock.self), incomingEvents.value(0));
    }`);
  return { state, ...module };
}
```

### Movers: track, trigger, driver

`Mover` wraps a named real object. `toMotionData()` reads its `AnimationClip` into
rows; `toMoverData(rest)` adds the numeric local collision/rest declaration and
fixed driver hash/input. The example is a Template-style vertical door with a
separate pendulum, not a claim that every animated mesh has physics.

```ts
import { Group, AnimationClip, VectorKeyframeTrack } from 'three';
import { Mover } from '@wildshard/sdk/movers';

/** Template-style moving door: two local positions and an explicit interaction trigger. */
export function moversExample() {
  const body = new Group(); body.name = 'template.door';
  const clip = new AnimationClip('door.open', 1, [
    new VectorKeyframeTrack('template.door.position', [0, 1], [0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 0]),
  ]);
  const door = new Mover(body, { clip, loop: 'once', trigger: { kind: 'interact', permission: 0 }, driver: { kind: 'track' } });
  const pendulumBody = new Group(); pendulumBody.name = 'template.pendulum';
  const pendulum = new Mover(pendulumBody, { trigger: { kind: 'always' }, driver: { kind: 'pendulum', axis: 'z', amplitude: 0.4, period: 3 } });
  const rest = { id: 'template.door', entity: 1, kind: 'platform' as const,
    at: { x: 0, y: 0, z: -8 }, euler: { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 }, enabled: true,
    boxes: [{ x: 0, y: 1.5, z: 0, hx: 1, hy: 1.5, hz: 0.2, rot: { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0, w: 1 } }] };
  return { door: door.toMoverData(rest), pendulum: pendulum.toMotionData() };
}
```

A track animates its own body's position and/or quaternion with LINEAR keys,
including time 0 and the exact duration, at most 10 shared times. `loop` is
`once`, `repeat` or `pingpong`; `speed` multiplies playback. Triggers are `always`,
`interact` (permission 0 or 3), `stand` (delay) or `shared` (field/equals).
Drivers are `static`, `track`, `pendulum`, `winch` (`mode: 'ride'` or `'hinge'`) or `waves`.
A pendulum declares axis, amplitude in radians and period in seconds and has no
clip. Track requires a clip. The winch drivers accept their fixed two-stop layouts;
waves/static have no clip and use `always`. Invalid combinations refuse.
`compileMoverDriver('clip'|'ride'|'hinge'|'waves')` produces the actual admitted
fixed Wasm asset; publish those hash-addressed bytes in the product rather than
inventing a module hash. Local boxes/chains, aggregate body limits and the
row's executable ABI are validated together.

### Player modes: zipline, updraft, ride, grapple

All four are ordinary `Object3D` declarations. `Zipline` and `Updraft` have local
endpoint vectors, lowered through their world transforms. `Mount` emits ordered
walk/trot/canter/gallop speeds; `Grapple` emits bounded range and timing controls.
`toModeData()` yields rows for `modes.traverse`,
`modes.ride` and `modes.grapple`. `readScene(scene)` collects these objects into
its admitted `modes` section in traversal order, including parent-transformed
endpoints. No mode objects means no `modes` key. The example is a Template-sized
demonstration.

```ts
import { Scene, Vector3 } from 'three';
import { Zipline, Updraft, Mount, Grapple } from '@wildshard/sdk/modes';
import { readScene } from '@wildshard/sdk/scene';
import { parseModes } from '@wildshard/format/modes';

/** Template-sized demonstration of all four control declarations; it grants no mount or anchors. */
export function modesExample() {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cable = new Zipline(new Vector3(0, 8, 0), new Vector3(12, 0, 0)); cable.name = 'template.cable';
  const wind = new Updraft(new Vector3(0, 0, 0), new Vector3(0, 10, 8), { width: 3, lift: 5 }); wind.name = 'template.wind';
  const mount = new Mount({ walk: 2, trot: 4, canter: 7, gallop: 10 }); mount.name = 'template.ride';
  const grapple = new Grapple(); grapple.name = 'template.grapple';
  scene.add(cable, wind, mount, grapple);
  const data = readScene(scene);
  if (data.modes === undefined) throw new Error('Missing authored mode rows');
  return { rows: parseModes(data.modes), scene: data };
}
```

Cable endpoints are floor positions; sag/hang are separate parameters. Updraft
is board-only and needs a horizontal run, width, lift and upper ceiling. Mount
profiles neither spawn nor tame a creature. Grapple profiles neither invent
anchors nor grant targets/floors. Native player/body/input owners must bind these
controls, and full admission proves their world/entry references.

### Weapon profiles and legacy weaponFamily

An optional weapon item's `profile` carries one `family` discriminator: `melee`,
`bow`, `firearm`, `thrown` or the additional `lash` contact profile. The item
family must explicitly accept that profile kind before allocation. A missing
profile retains the existing family rule. These four small examples are
illustrative numeric data for a Template-style equipment catalogue; they do not
change a shipped weapon.

```ts
import { parseWeaponProfile } from '@wildshard/format/weaponProfiles';

/** Small bounded profiles for a Template-style equipment catalogue; native families own contacts and views. */
export function weaponsExample() {
  return [
    parseWeaponProfile({ family: 'melee', damage: 10, reach: 2, swingScale: 1, cooldown: 0.4,
      comboGap: 0.5, chainLag: 0.1, heavyCharge: 0.6,
      moves: { combo: [{ windup: 0.1, slashEnd: 0.2, total: 0.4, damage: 1 }], heavy: { windup: 0.2, slashEnd: 0.4, total: 0.7, damage: 2 } },
      lunge: { range: 3, heavyRange: 4, cone: 1, stop: 1, speed: 4, minTime: 0.1, maxTime: 0.4 },
      sweep: { rays: 3, extensions: [1], step: 0.1, maxSamples: 16, maxHits: 8 } }),
    parseWeaponProfile({ family: 'bow', quiver: 24, speedBase: 30, speedDraw: 28, damageScale: 1.2,
      draw: { drawTime: 0.8, letdownTime: 0.2, renockTime: 0.6, renockEarly: 0.5, holdSteady: 1, holdTire: 3, tiredTime: 1 },
      spread: { degrees: 1, radius: 'sqrt', axisScale: 1, aimMultiplier: 0.5, motion: 1 },
      flight: { gravity: 9.8, drag: 0.01, windCoupling: 1 }, muzzle: 0.5, pool: 32, substeps: 4, lifetime: 10 }),
    parseWeaponProfile({ family: 'firearm', action: 'semi', magazine: 6, reserve: 24, interval: 0.3,
      reload: 1.5, reloadMode: 'magazine', autoReload: 0, damageScale: 1, range: 80,
      spreadAds: 0.5, spreadHip: 3, spreadRadius: 'sqrt', bloomShot: 0.2, bloomMax: 2, movingSpread: 1, movingAimReduction: 0.5,
      projectile: { kind: 'bullet', delivery: 'hitscan', speed: 100, radius: 0.01,
        flight: { gravity: 0, drag: 0, windCoupling: 0 }, pool: 16, substeps: 1, lifetime: 1 } }),
    parseWeaponProfile({ family: 'thrown', speed: 20, gravity: 9.8, damage: 20, headMultiplier: 2,
      radius: 0.1, headOffset: 0.2, windup: 0.2, release: 0.1, recovery: 0.5,
      carried: 3, pool: 8, pickupRadius: 1, pickupHeight: 1, survive: 1, arcPoints: 8, arcAfter: 0.2, stagger: 1 }),
  ];
}
```

Melee declares ordered swings, combo/heavy timing, lunges and sweep limits. Bow
declares draw/fatigue, spread and flight. Firearm declares magazine/reload,
semi/lever/bolt action, optional lever clocks and hitscan/flight projectile data.
Thrown declares windup/release/recovery, finite pool and walk-over pickup values.
Lash declares ordered unroll/second/show timing, pulls/stagger and named moves.
Views, audio, contacts, aim, ammunition and native continuations retain their
real owners. Profiles are not arbitrary new weapon algorithms.

Only a legacy `runtime/` imports
`@wildshard/engine/game/plugin/weaponFamily.registerWeaponFamily`. It registers an
existing weapon constructor in a caller-owned session registry, with a bounded
shard-local name; duplicate/reserved names and tool constructors refuse. Signal
and Sky use this for their native lash/fan. An author row naming a family does
not install a constructor. This typed runtime example deliberately takes the
real existing family instead of replacing its implementation.

```ts
import { registerWeaponFamily } from '@wildshard/engine/game/plugin/weaponFamily';

/** runtime/ only: register an existing constructor in the explicit session-local registry. */
export function weaponFamilyExample(
  registry: Parameters<typeof registerWeaponFamily>[0],
  existingFamily: Parameters<typeof registerWeaponFamily>[2],
) {
  registerWeaponFamily(registry, 'template.practice', existingFamily);
  return registry;
}
```

### Brain archetypes, presets and boss rows

The five parametric decision families are stalker, guardian, grazer, diver and
boss. Existing names are presets with preserved save labels, not aliases that
change traces. Pattern-specific data must go with the real body's home, shared
RNG, navigation, strike, contact and flight ports. A parsed catalogue is not a
new actor or an attack permission. Template 1's actual pursuit/spawn example
below is the smaller generic creature path; the held boss is a minimal
illustrative declaration for its existing big-blob owner.

```ts
import * as v from 'valibot';
import { CreaturesSchema } from '@wildshard/format/creatures';
import { parseBossProfile } from '@wildshard/format/bossProfiles';

/** Template 1's actual pursuit row/spawn, plus a minimal held-body boss declaration. */
export function brainsExample() {
  const creatures = v.parse(CreaturesSchema, {
    brains: [{ id: 'blob-pursuit', kind: 'pursue', awareRadius: 12, leashRadius: 25, speed: 1, returnSpeed: 2,
      stopDistance: 1.5, turnRate: 4, thinkDivisor: 3, attackCooldownTicks: 60, wanderRadius: 4, wanderEveryTicks: 420 }],
    spawns: [{ id: 'grey-blob:1', species: 'grey-blob', variant: 'grey', brain: 'blob-pursuit', strike: null, seed: 435, scale: 1, at: [0, 0, -19], yaw: 0 }],
  });
  const boss = parseBossProfile({ kind: 'boss', pattern: 'held', fight: {
    arena: { x: -15, z: -20, r: 10, floor: 0 }, hpShares: [1, 0.5],
    rewardPoint: { x: -15, y: 0, z: -18 }, respawn: { x: -15, y: 0, z: -12, yaw: 0 },
  } });
  return { creatures, boss };
}
```

| Archetype | Pattern / existing preset |
|---|---|
| stalker | `skirmish` / skirmisher; pack-group hunting |
| guardian | `interior` / guardian; `perch` / perch-hunter |
| grazer | `wander-ram` / ram-grazer; `circle-challenge` / challenge-grazer; herd-group grazing |
| diver | `orbit` / orbit-diver; `patrol` / patrol-diver; `burst` / burst-flyer |
| boss | `arena`, `roaming`, `spawned`, `held`, `script` |

Use the defining `brains`, `grazers`, `flyers`, `groupBrains` and `bossProfiles`
format parsers (or their SDK data constructors) before building a catalogue.
Named strikes must resolve. The boss row keeps the selected fight pattern's
phase thresholds, modes, attacks, rewards and continuation; the host must bind
that exact pattern. Script bosses wrap an admitted elite-script module, slots,
contacts and action order. A held boss keeps its actual body identity; a spawned
boss explicitly owns creation/checkpoint shares. Unsupported one-shard laws
remain legacy tails: Sky's phased-raptor is not silently a phased-flyer, and
Pine's animated hit timing/weather gaps are not closed by a schema parse.

### Shared content from kit

`@wildshard/kit` contains shared creature content and author helpers.
A build copies the selected content into the one shard format. A shard may
use its own look; changing a kit version changes a shard only when rebuilt.
Models, clips and sounds remain ordinary immutable files with their retained
authored inputs. See the kit GUIDE for plain GLBs and TypeScript builders.

```ts
import { quadruped } from '@wildshard/kit/body';
import { temperament } from '@wildshard/kit/temperament';

/** Each rebuild copies plain kit content; a shard may supply its own look. */
export function kitContentExample() {
  return {
    body: quadruped({ look: 'meadow.look.boar', size: 'medium', scale: 1 }),
    temperament: temperament.neutral(),
  };
}
```

## Data-only herds and divers

The ordinary client and `HeadlessSimulation` install herd/grazer-herd and orbit/patrol-diver recipes for
a shard with no legacy runtime. Declare real species/variants, ordered group members and a sphere strike.
No `runtime/` installer or game import is needed. The recipe reads native world LOS and ground slope,
the player's measured speed, the host's shared `ai` RNG and attack authorization; the existing flight motor
and strike/contact pipeline move and damage. Per-host motion and policy clocks restore with the world.
There is no inferred cover, wind/scent, taming, pack interaction or audible cue binding; those need their
explicit owners. Legacy injected recipes retain precedence. Pack, burst and other specialized recipes still
refuse when no native owner is supplied. This example declares no rendered rig; creature view proof is separate.

```ts
import { compileBehaviourModule } from '@wildshard/sdk/buildBehaviour';
import { emptyShardfile } from '@wildshard/sdk/author';
import { parseShardfile } from '@wildshard/format/shardSchema';

/** Data-only goats flee through the guarded-herd owner; a hawk dives through the native flight/contact owner. */
export function creaturesExample() {
  const shard = emptyShardfile({ slug: 'mesa-fauna', name: 'Mesa fauna', author: 'Example', revision: 1, seed: 435 });
  const dims = { bodyY: 0.8, bodyHalfLen: 0.6, bodyRadius: 0.3, headRadius: 0.2,
    legLen: 0.6, feet: [[0.2, 0.3], [-0.2, -0.3]] as [number, number][], halfWidth: 0.3 };
  const mods = { speed: 1, chargeDist: 1, damageTaken: 1, chargeDamage: 5, relentless: false };
  const variants = [{ id: 'plain', label: 'Plain', rarity: 'common' as const, weight: 1,
    scale: [1, 1] as [number, number], hp: 60, mods }];
  shard.rows.species = [
    { id: 'goat', kind: 'goat', label: 'Goat', aggressive: false, lockable: true, dims, variants },
    { id: 'hawk', kind: 'hawk', label: 'Hawk', aggressive: true, lockable: true, dims, variants,
      flight: { altitude: 8, above: 'world', climbRate: 8, diveRate: 20 } },
  ];
  shard.rows.strikes = [{ id: 'hawk.dive', shape: { kind: 'sphere', radius: 2 },
    windup: 0.2, active: 0.6, recover: 0.3, cooldown: 2, range: 12, damage: 5,
    tags: ['animal.hawk'], weight: 1, speed: 0 }];
  shard.creatures.groups = [{ id: 'goats', kind: 'grazer', pattern: 'herd', thinkDivisor: 6,
    members: ['goat.0', 'goat.1', 'goat.2'], walkSpeed: 1, trotSpeed: 3, gallopSpeed: 7, chargeSpeed: 8,
    sightRadius: 25, grazingSightRadius: 18, coneAngle: Math.PI, hearing: [10, 16, 24, 30],
    alertThreshold: 0.5, flightMinDistance: 25, flightMaxDistance: 40,
    stallionVariant: 'guard', foalPrefix: 'kid', snortCue: 'goat.snort', neighCue: 'goat.call', squealCue: 'goat.alarm' }];
  shard.creatures.brains = [{ id: 'hawk', kind: 'diver', pattern: 'orbit', thinkDivisor: 6, strike: 'hawk.dive',
    home: { x: 0, z: 0, r: 10, y: 8 }, circleSpeed: 5, hangAltitude: 4, stalkSpeed: 8, diveSpeed: 12,
    restSeconds: 3, noticeRadius: 35, giveUpRadius: 50, initialRestSeconds: 0, stalkMaxSeconds: 20,
    riseMargin: 2, targetHeight: 1.2, alignRadius: 3, alignTolerance: 1 }];
  shard.creatures.spawns = [0, 1, 2].map(i => ({ id: `goat.${i}`, species: 'goat', variant: 'plain',
    brain: 'goats', strike: null, seed: i, scale: 1, at: [i * 2 + 4, 0, 0] as [number, number, number], yaw: 0 }));
  shard.creatures.spawns.push({ id: 'hawk.0', species: 'hawk', variant: 'plain', brain: 'hawk',
    strike: null, seed: 9, scale: 1, at: [0, 8, 4], yaw: 0 });
  return parseShardfile(shard);
}

/** Give the data-only roster real existing platform primitive views; declaration-only creatures fail view proofs. */
export function visibleCreaturesExample() {
  const shard = creaturesExample();
  shard.rows.looks = shard.rows.species.map(row => ({ id: `look.${row.id}`, species: row.id, recipe: 'engine.sphere',
    parameters: { radius: 0.5, colour: [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] }, material: null,
    animation: { recipe: 'engine.scale-wave', parameters: { axis: 'y', frequency: 4, amplitude: 0.08, rest: 1, dead: 0.4 } } }));
  return parseShardfile(shard);
}

/** Compile an event-controlled beacon beside the live primitive views, using only public author modules. */
export async function sceneInteractionExample(source: string) {
  const shard = visibleCreaturesExample();
  shard.state.shared = [{ id: 101, name: 'door.open', type: 'bool', privacy: 'public', default: false }];
  shard.sim.scriptTickDivisor = 1;
  const { bytes, module } = await compileBehaviourModule(source, 2);
  const resident = bytes.length + 2 * 65536 * 3;
  shard.files = [{ hash: module, kind: 'wasm', compressed: bytes.length, decoded: bytes.length, gpu: 0, triangles: 0, draws: 0, dependencies: [], critical: true }];
  shard.critical = [module];
  shard.budgets.sim = { resident, compressed: bytes.length };
  shard.serverBudget.memory += resident;
  shard.sim.scripts = [module];
  shard.sim.bindings = [{ module, entity: 1106943697, actorId: 'actor.player', kind: 'server' }];
  shard.hooks.scenes = [{ id: 'beacon.light', type: 201, value: 1 }];
  shard.targets.interactions = [{ id: 'beacon', at: [0, 1.68, 1], radius: 3, label: 'LIGHT BEACON', scene: 'beacon.light' }];
  return { shard: parseShardfile(shard), assets: new Map([[module, bytes]]) };
}
```

## Install outside the workspace

Use the [standalone author setup](standalone-author.md) for matched SDK/format release archives,
local CLI scripts, ordinary immutable assets and the retained readable TypeScript world generator. Bootstrap
preserves installed dependencies and refuses existing authored files; no checkout link is an installation proof.

## Equip the author template's starter spear

The retained `generators/spear.ts` owns the readable static spear model
and item rows. Its generator writes the GLB as an ordinary immutable file;
`shard.config.ts` declares its measured cost, includes it in `library`, and
copies the item rows into the shard. No catalogue compiler or separate
shared-content endpoint is needed. The native proof checks the exact file
hash and equipped row before running the simulation and client proofs.

This spear thrusts and performs a charged heavy thrust. Its static model has
no textures, rig or clips, and does not claim mounted or throwing behavior.

```ts
import { starterSpearContent } from '../author-project/generators/spear';
import { emptyShardfile } from '@wildshard/sdk/author';
import { parseShardfile, type Shardfile } from '@wildshard/format/shardSchema';

/** The retained spear is ordinary item rows plus one content-addressed model file. */
export function spearExample(slug = 'spear-outpost'): { source: Shardfile; assets: ReadonlyMap<string, Uint8Array> } {
  const spear = starterSpearContent();
  const shard = emptyShardfile({ slug, name: 'Spear outpost', author: 'Example', revision: 1, seed: 435 });
  shard.items = spear.items;
  shard.files = [{ hash: spear.hash, kind: 'glb', compressed: spear.model.length, decoded: spear.cost.decoded, gpu: spear.cost.gpu, triangles: spear.cost.triangles, draws: spear.cost.draws, dependencies: [], critical: false }];
  shard.library = [spear.hash];
  shard.budgets.library = { resident: spear.cost.decoded + spear.cost.gpu, compressed: spear.model.length };
  return { source: parseShardfile(shard), assets: new Map([[spear.hash, spear.model]]) };
}
```

## Export named model parts (OS-G6)

`staticGlb` emits one glTF node per primitive. Its optional per-primitive `name`
is the stable name for interactions and presentation bindings; the overall name
is only the fallback. Explicit names must be unique and loader-safe (letters,
digits, underscore or hyphen; at most 128 characters). Duplicate or sanitized
names refuse export. Unnamed existing exports retain their exact bytes.

```ts
import { BoxGeometry, Group, Mesh, MeshStandardMaterial } from 'three';
import { clientSceneGlb, staticGlb } from '@wildshard/sdk/bake/glb';

/** Export separately addressable tower/flame nodes without merging their geometry or changing material identity. */
export function namedNodesExample() {
  const tower = new BoxGeometry(1, 4, 1), flame = new BoxGeometry(0.3, 0.5, 0.3);
  const stone = new MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x888888 }), fire = new MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xff7700 });
  try {
    return staticGlb([
      { name: 'beacon-tower', geometry: tower, material: stone },
      { name: 'beacon-flame', geometry: flame, material: fire },
    ], 'beacon');
  } finally { tower.dispose(); flame.dispose(); stone.dispose(); fire.dispose(); }
}

/** Bake the existing V1 scene declaration beside exact local geometry; the client lends the original material. */
export function namedSceneExample() {
  const root = new Group(), paint = new MeshStandardMaterial(), geometry = new BoxGeometry(1, 2, 1), mesh = new Mesh(geometry, paint);
  root.name = 'beacon'; mesh.name = 'tower'; root.add(mesh);
  try { return clientSceneGlb(root, new Map([[paint, 'stone']])); }
  finally { geometry.dispose(); paint.dispose(); }
}
```

The named-node example also emits an exact rest hierarchy with
`clientSceneGlb`: the existing V1 scene rows and mesh-local GLB accessors are
separate outputs. Materials are named client ports, not copies of shader
code. A declared model-library geometry pool preserves original Float32
channels, index width, groups and bounds; `geometry(id)` lends independent
owned copies to `createClientScene`. Unsupported geometry refuses rather
than converting or refitting it.
